- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price drop is steep.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply early correction (day 2–4) to align with sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical reversion.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative signals, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70, model often misses the bottom; add 1–3% buffer to prevent undershoot.
